entities.name: PMID:25423126
observations: In the rat Noble–Collip drum trauma model, immediate and 30-minute samples showed spontaneous thrombin bursts, approximately 50-fold higher soluble fibrin, consumption of platelets/coagulation factors/antithrombin, hyperfibrin(ogen)olysis, and no change in activated protein C; authors concluded fibrinolytic DIC, not ACoTS.

entities.name: PMID:34645889
observations: In a separate rat Noble–Collip blunt-trauma study, immediate hypotension, lactic acidosis, hemoconcentration, increased soluble fibrin, and increased tPA were followed by rapid PAI-1-mediated suppression of fibrinolysis; the model produces shock and dynamic coagulofibrinolysis.

entities.name: Noble–Collip DIC phenotype
observations: The model is best classified as trauma-associated DIC with a fibrinolytic phenotype: systemic thrombin generation, consumptive loss of platelets/factors/antithrombin, endothelial injury markers, and fibrin(ogen)olysis are documented.
The principal direct study found no activated-protein-C increase and explicitly concluded that the model did not induce ACoTS.
